Cherish

/CHAIR-ish/ - rhymes with perish · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Cherish means to treasure and hold dear.

Long after the band broke up, the drummer cherished the setlist the four of them had signed on the last night of the tour.

Worked Example

The cliff path above the village is nothing special to look at — a muddy track, a bent handrail. But the villagers' grandparents went to court three times to keep it public, and the whole village walks it every autumn in their honor. Ask anyone repainting that handrail why, and you will hear the same word: ours.

Cherish is the exact word for how the village holds that path, because cherish means to treasure and hold dear — the worth lives in the heart, not the price. Value is the cooler cousin: you can value a thing for what it fetches; you cherish it for what it means.

How Cherish Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

treasure

treasure: to guard as precious — nearly a twin; treasure leans on worth, cherish on warmth

prize

prize: to value highly, often for usefulness or rarity

Antonyms

scorn

scorn: to reject as beneath notice

discard

discard: to toss out as trash

How Strong Is It? — value → cherish → adore

value vs. cherish

value vs. cherish: Valuing something can be pure arithmetic — an appraiser values a car without feeling a thing for it.

adore vs. cherish

adore vs. cherish: Adore goes further than cherish — adoration gazes up at its object, while cherishing folds a thing close and keeps it safe.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — cher

Root — cher: dear (French cher, from Latin carus)

Suffix — -ish

Suffix — -ish: verb ending, from French -iss-

Put it together

Put it together: Cher (dear) + -ish (verb ending) = to hold dear. French cherir carried Latin carus, 'dear, precious,' into English, and the meaning never drifted: to cherish something is to treat it as dear — priced by the heart rather than the market.

Use the root in a new word: charity

Use the root in a new word: charity: Charity comes from the same 'dear' root — giving that treats strangers as dear, because they matter and not because they can repay it.

Root Check

Word Choice

warm / tender

Cherish is for what the heart has adopted: a person, a keepsake, a right, a memory. Its unit-mates care differently — nurture feeds something so it grows, and foster builds the conditions around it; cherish asks for no growth at all, only holding dear. If money could stand in for the thing, cherish is probably too big a word.
